title: God fills all things; the water of forgetfulness is a myth
english: God fills all things and is limited by no one. For the one who is not limited by place will certainly be in every place, according to the hymnody of David. If he were said to be outside some place, he would necessarily be limited by that very place of which he is deprived. Being wholly present in all things, then, he does not move from one place to another, since he fills all things.
The divine is not subject to fixed circumscriptions of laws and times.

But since they clearly know that they are caught by this, they change course and fabricate the water of forgetfulness, which they say each person drinks and thereby forgets the births of their former lives. That these things are mythical and far from philosophy, no one of sound mind seems to be ignorant. For what do we say, Pythagoreans and Platonists? Have you yourselves taken and drunk the water of forgetfulness?
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius opens his treatise by addressing Pythagorean and Platonist philosophers, first establishing that God is not confined by place, then attacking their myth of the water of forgetfulness.
